SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT, KALABURAGI IN MVC NO.587/2024 AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION TO RS.8,96,100 PAYABLE WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 9%
PER ANNUM IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE.
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS

, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant against the Judgment and award dated 07.03.2025 passed in MVC No.587/2024 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and I Additional Senior Civil Judge,
Kalaburagi (for short 'the tribunal') seeking enhancement of the compensation.
2. The claimant met with accident on 12.08.2017 and suffered grievous injuries.
He filed claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.18,50,000/-.

The tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, NC: 2025:KHC-K:7385 HC-KAR awarded a sum of Rs.9,53,900/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

Being aggrieved by the said Judgment and award, the claimant has preferred the present appeal and mainly contended that, he was earning a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and Rs.200/- per day as batta and he incurred medical expenses of Rs.4,50,000, but the tribunal without considering the same has awarded meager compensation and requests for enhancement of the compensation.
3. Heard the arguments from both sides.
4. The claimant has not filed any income proof to show his income.
He met with accident on 12.08.2017.
Hence, the tribunal has rightly taken the income of the claimant at Rs.10,250/-.
The claimant was aged 25 years and the multiplier is '18'.

The claimant sustained four plate with ten screws used for open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) of fracture of roof, medical and posterolateral wall of right orbit, anterior medial and posterolateral wall of bilateral maxillary sinus,
Neminath vs Kantilal on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73571374/
2
bilateral pterygoid plates, right zygomatic NC: 2025:KHC-K:7385 HC-KAR arch, right posterior wall of condylar fosa and floor of right orbit.
As per the discharge summary, the claimant was hospitalized for 39 days.
P.W.2 the Doctor issued disability certificate under Ex.P.12.
He assessed the permanent disability of the claimant at 28% to maxillofacial region.
He further stated that, the approximate expenditure to restore the malocclusion and replacement and to restore the affected teeth would be Rs.1,52,300/-.
The tribunal has considered the disability of the claimant at 15%.
Considering the nature of injury and period of hospitalization, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the said order.
5. The tribunal also added 40% of the income towards future prospects and assessed the loss of future income at Rs.9,53,900/- and it is confirmed.
The tribunal also awarded a sum of Rs.2,20,000/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
6. Since, the amounts granted by the tribunal under different heads are correct and reasonable, this Court finds no reason to interfere in the said order.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7385 HC-KAR 7.
It is submitted that, the compensation amount awarded by the tribunal is already deposited before the tribunal.
The claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount along with interest accrued on it.
8. In the result, the appeal is dismissed confirming the Judgment and order of the tribunal.
